issue.title: gateway: a Responses upstream cut after the reply began ends the turn; no continuation path (prefillHow is empty for Responses)
issue.body:
## Summary

When a **Responses (OpenAI/Codex-style) upstream** drops the stream after the reply has started, Claude Code gets `API Error: Server error mid-response. The response above may be incomplete.` and the turn ends. For a **subagent** (Agent tool) that is the whole task: the parent receives only that error. Sending the subagent a plain "continue" almost always finishes the work, so the failure is recoverable, but nothing in Magpie does it.

`continuation.go` already re-asks a cut reply with the shown part sent back, but only where the upstream can go on from a prefilled reply. On current main:

```go
// internal/gateway/continuation.go:212
func prefillHow(p provider.Provider, to provider.Protocol, model string) string {
	switch to {
	case provider.Anthropic:
		return "anthropic"
	case provider.Chat:
		return chatPrefill(p.Host(), model)
	}
	return ""
}
```

A Responses upstream returns `""`, so a cut after the first word ends with the error (`connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)`). I found no open or closed issue about this case: #1418/#1748 are the before-first-byte "at capacity" case (handled by Patience), #2243 is Anthropic `end_turn` (declined, with good reasons), #2136 is Pi.

## Environment

- Magpie 0.1.1308, Windows; Claude Code 2.1.306 as the client, calling a routing group of `gpt-6.1-sol` members (one Codex account plus several OpenAI-compatible relays) through the Responses-to-Anthropic translation.
- The cuts come from the relays and, less often, the Codex account: `connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)` after `firstText`, 40 to 128 s into the reply.

## Evidence (my own routing logs and transcripts, 2026-10-19 to 10-21)

- Routing log, claude agent, `gpt-6.1-sol` group: 18 attempts (about 12.5k requests in the three days) were cut with `mid-reply ... unexpected EOF` after text had started; 17 of them were relays, 1 the Codex account. The request itself is logged as 200 because the HTTP status had already gone out. Most other 502/529/429 attempts failed before any text and were absorbed by failover or Patience, so those are not the problem.
- Claude Code subagent transcripts since 10-20: 58 subagents ended with an `API Error` message. 36 were resumed afterwards by the parent sending "continue". 22 were not (some are 403 balance errors, which are a different case).
- Timestamps line up: the routing-log cuts at 10-20 17:21 to 17:33 (UTC+8) match `Server error mid-response` in the subagent transcripts at 09:35 UTC.

## What would help (any one of these)

1. **Opt-in continuation for Responses upstreams**: when the reply was cut after text and before any tool call began, re-ask with the shown text as the assistant item plus a short "continue exactly from here" user item, and stream the answer as the rest of the same reply. This is the same safety rule `continuation.go` already uses (no tool call begun, bounded by `streamRetries`), and it is off by default, so it does not tell the client a cut reply is a whole one (the objection to #2243). Splicing a reworded answer is the real risk here, which is why I suggest opt-in per group.
2. If (1) is not acceptable: when a cut cannot be continued, end it with an error type and wording the client treats as retryable, and say in the routing detail that output had already been delivered. I have not verified whether Claude Code retries on that, so this is a question rather than a claim.

Not asked: replaying anything after a tool call has begun, or unlimited retries.

## Where to look

- `internal/gateway/continuation.go`: `prefillHow`, `streamRetries`, `errEndedShort`.
- `internal/gateway/patience.go`: covers the before-first-byte case only ("nothing of a reply has gone to the agent").

comments.body:
Root cause: `prefillHow` (`internal/gateway/continuation.go`) returned `""` for every Responses upstream, so a reply the upstream cut after text began had no continuation path at all — the same cut that Anthropic and Chat upstreams get re-asked with a prefill ended the turn with "the reply ended before it was complete".

Fix (fork branch, on top of current main 8abdf53a8):

- `prefillHow` returns a new `continueMode` for Responses: that upstream takes no prefill (a conversation ending with the assistant's message is a turn already said), so the cut reply is re-asked with the shown part sent back as the conversation's last assistant message plus a user turn asking the model on — the same `continueText` a model that takes no prefill is already asked with (`prefill.go`). Nothing is put in the model's mouth that the client doesn't already have.
- Asked exactly once, not `streamRetries` times: the model may answer anew, so the shown part goes back only that one time (`TestStreamCutResponsesContinuesOnlyOnce`).
- The existing safety rule is unchanged: only a reply no tool call has begun, the vendor's refusal and the request's own 400 end it as before; a cut before anything was shown stays the empty reply's to answer (`TestStreamCutBeforeFirstByteResponsesNotContinued`).

One deliberate difference from your option 1: this is not opt-in per group — it rides the same always-on rule `continuation.go` already uses for Anthropic/Chat prefill continuation, bounded to a single re-ask. If the maintainer prefers opt-in, the mode is one switch to flip.

Verification (GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8):

- `TestStreamCutMidReplyContinuesOnResponses` (cut after "Let me look at the", second ask carries the shown part back as the assistant's turn plus the user turn, client reads one whole reply with 1 start / 1 stop / 0 errors) and `TestStreamCutResponsesContinuesOnlyOnce`: red on clean main 8abdf53a8, green on the branch. `TestPrefillHow` updated.
- The `Continu|Prefill|Cut|EndedShort|HalfLine|KeepAlive|Hold` neighborhood and the full `./internal/gateway` package pass, except `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged` which fails on clean main on this machine too (local Claude cache present), and `TestCodexPoolSaysTheClientsVersion`, order-dependent, passes alone on both trees. gofmt / vet / build clean.

Not verified: against a real Responses relay or Codex account (no such upstream here — the tests run against a scripted upstream), no `-race`, and the routing-page view of the re-ask.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3166-responses-continuation (head `08a2d1f5`)

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.

issue.title: Codex provider disappears and the account is turned off after a 12m mid-reply EOF; group member becomes "not served"

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Environment

- magpie `0.1.2926` (latest at the time), Linux aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04
- Codex account: ChatGPT **Plus** (`r***@gmail.com`), signed in through magpie's OAuth flow (`magpie accounts add codex`), not `accounts import`
- Group `claude-plan`: `claude/claude-opus-5-5:xhigh → codex/gpt-6.1-sol:max → kimi/k3.1-pro:max → group/exec`, `routing=order`, `stays=auto`
- Network: the machine reaches OpenAI through a LAN proxy; `auth.openai.com` / `chatgpt.com` `/cdn-cgi/trace` shows `loc=US`

### Symptom

After a Codex request ran for **12m26s** and ended with `200 ... Codex: connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)`, the `codex` provider disappeared and the account was left off:

- `magpie accounts codex --json`: `active: false`, `on: false`, quota **5h 64% / 7d 10%** (not exhausted)
- `magpie provider codex`: `no provider "codex"`
- `magpie group claude-plan`: member `codex/gpt-6.1-sol:max` → `not served: no provider codex now, skipped`
- `magpie accounts switch codex r***@gmail.com` re-signed the **same** account and the provider came back without a restart; a small request then returned `200 OK`.

Relevant log lines:

```text
20:33:40 gateway: claude's call to group/claude-plan on codex failed: 499 after 4.318s: the agent canceled the request
20:56:46 gateway: claude's call to group/claude-plan on codex failed: 499 after 23.613s: the agent canceled the request
21:23:14 gateway: claude's call to group/claude-plan on codex failed: 200 after 12m26.172s: Codex: connection lost mid-reply (unexpected EOF)
```

The first two are the agent canceling. The third is the important one: the group was on the Codex member, the upstream stream ended mid-reply, and afterwards the provider was gone.

### Questions

1. Is turning the account/provider **off** after a mid-reply EOF intended? Is there a setting to keep the account on and let the group fail over to the next member instead of removing the provider?
2. For a group with `routing=order`, how can I bound how long a member may take before the next member is tried? The old `smart-split` group had `firstToken: 30` in `providers.json`, but `magpie group set claude-plan firstToken=60` returns `unknown field "firstToken"`. Is that field UI-only, or is there a supported CLI/config way?
3. For `codex/gpt-6.1-sol:max` that occasionally takes >10 minutes and then EOFs, what is the recommended mitigation — lower effort (`:high`), a provider `patience` setting, a group rule, or wait for #3166?

Related issues: #4425 (import not truly detached from `~/.codex/auth.json`; after `codex logout` the magpie account is invalid), #3166 (Responses upstream cut mid-reply has no continuation path), #4934 (a plugin stream silent past 5 minutes now ends instead of hanging).

I can attach a `magpie log` bundle or the usage CSV if useful.
